project_requirements.title: What the call wants
project_requirements.question: What must the project address, develop and achieve?

cards.title: Central object
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop?
cards.answer:
A next-generation battery concept beyond the state of the art, based on innovative advanced materials, in one of three areas: low-cost, high-performance, or stationary storage.
Area A is low-cost batteries for electric cars and/or stationary storage; Area B is high-performance batteries for aviation and maritime use; Area C is durable advanced materials and cell concepts for stationary storage in grids or energy-intensive industry. Each project contributes to one area only.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 101–105 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-04-Two-Stage-D2-07, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: Scope
cards.question: Which activities fall within the funding opportunity's scope?
cards.answer:
Projects choose one area and cover its points, plus three assessments that apply to all.
Area A — low-cost batteries:
- chemistries with minimal critical raw materials; cost reduction through smart functions and lighter or simpler casing or cooling is encouraged
Area B — high-performance batteries:
- structural integration and multifunctional materials to boost weight and volume performance
Area C — stationary storage materials and cells:
- for grid storage: potential for cost-effective system integration, targeting a system cost below EUR 50 per kWh, and support for multi-hour storage to enhance renewable uptake and grid flexibility
- for energy-intensive industry: continuous high-load operation, cycling in harsh conditions and long-term reliability
All projects must assess:
- scalability, manufacturability and market relevance
- extended cycle life, cost-efficient recyclability and sustainability by design
- safety, thermal management, performance monitoring and predictive diagnostics
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 101–105 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-04-Two-Stage-D2-07, Scope

cards.title: Problem
cards.question: What type of problem or need must justify the project, and where must it originate?
cards.answer:
Europe needs new battery concepts and materials to stay competitive and support clean energy use, from cheap EV cells to grid-scale storage.
The need originates with industry and the energy system: battery cost, performance and dependence on critical raw materials limit electric mobility and storage. For Area C the need lies with grid operators and energy-intensive industry needing durable, affordable multi-hour storage.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 101–105 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-04-Two-Stage-D2-07, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: Deliverables
cards.question: Which concrete outputs must the project produce?
cards.answer:
Validated battery concepts in the chosen area, with benchmarks against today's technology, and assessments of scalability, sustainability and safety.
- Area A: benchmark against state-of-the-art lithium-ion and sodium-ion batteries, and main component cost below EUR 35 per kWh
- Area B: validated concepts exceeding 500 Wh/kg energy density and/or state-of-the-art power density
- Area C: durable and reliable advanced materials and cell-level concepts for stationary storage
- For all: the three required assessments, and reports to the Batt4EU and IAM4EU partnerships
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 101–105 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-04-Two-Stage-D2-07, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: Impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer:
Projects are expected to generate innovative battery concepts that safeguard European competitiveness and support green energy use through better storage and energy management.
Each area has its own targets:
- Area A: main component cost below EUR 35 per kWh, compared against a state-of-the-art benchmark
- Area B: energy density above 500 Wh/kg and/or power density beyond the state of the art
- Area C: for grids, system-level cost below EUR 50 per kWh and multi-hour storage for renewable uptake and grid flexibility
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 101–105 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-04-Two-Stage-D2-07, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: After the project
cards.question: How must the result be replicated, taken up and kept in use after the project?
cards.answer:
Results stay at laboratory scale but must be assessed for scalability, manufacturability, market relevance and recyclability.
- The Safe and Sustainable by Design framework (an EU framework for safer and more sustainable chemicals and materials) should guide the work
- Reporting to the European Partnership on Batteries (Batt4EU) and the Innovative Advanced Materials partnership (IAM4EU) on their indicators
- The granting authority may object, for up to 4 years after the project, to a transfer of ownership or exclusive licensing of results
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 101–105 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-04-Two-Stage-D2-07, Specific conditions and Scope

cards.title: Number of partners
cards.question: What is the permitted or required consortium size?
cards.answer:
At least three independent organisations from three different countries; the call sets no maximum.
The general rule requires, as beneficiaries (organisations that sign the grant agreement and receive funding), three legal entities independent of each other: at least one established in an EU Member State and two others each in a different Member State or country associated with Horizon Europe (non-EU countries taking part in the programme, such as Norway, Switzerland or the United Kingdom). Affiliated entities (organisations legally linked to a beneficiary) and associated partners (organisations taking part without funding) do not count towards this minimum.
The European Commission's Joint Research Centre (JRC) may join the selected consortium, but does not count for the proposal since it does not take part in preparing it.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · B — Eligibility, Consortium composition
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 101–105 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-04-Two-Stage-D2-07

cards.title: Partner composition
cards.question: Which types of partners must the consortium include?
cards.answer:
The call names no required partner types; it invites proposals to consider involving the Joint Research Centre for battery performance or safety research.
The JRC would join after selection as a zero-funding beneficiary or associated partner. Legal entities established in China are not eligible for research and innovation actions in this part of the work programme.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 101–105 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-04-Two-Stage-D2-07, Specific conditions and Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 6–7 · B — Restrictions on the participation of legal entities established in China

cards.title: Distribution of work
cards.question: How must work and budget be distributed among partners?
cards.answer:
The call prescribes no division of work or budget.
Since the grant is a lump sum (a fixed amount paid against completed work packages), the consortium must allocate the amount to work packages and partners in a detailed budget table at the second stage.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 101–105 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-04-Two-Stage-D2-07, Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents, lump sum grant proposals

cards.title: Coordinator
cards.question: What type of organisation may or must act as lead applicant?
cards.answer:
No type of organisation is prescribed: the beneficiaries choose one of themselves as coordinator.
The coordinator manages and coordinates the project and represents the consortium towards the granting authority (the European Commission or its agency). At submission it must confirm that it has the mandate to act for all applicants.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Coordinator
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents, Submission

project_requirements.title: TenneT's position
project_requirements.question: What is TenneT's position within the consortium?

cards.title: Coordinate
cards.question: Can TenneT apply or coordinate, and under which conditions?
cards.answer:
Formally yes, but battery materials research is led by research institutes and battery industry; TenneT TSO B.V. would at most join an Area C consortium.
Any eligible beneficiary may coordinate, and a Dutch entity is eligible.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 11, 36 · B — Entities eligible for funding; IMPORTANT, Coordinator
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 101–105 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-04-Two-Stage-D2-07, Scope

cards.title: Participate
cards.question: Can TenneT take part without receiving funding?
cards.answer:
Yes, as an associated partner, which takes part without funding and bears its own costs.
An associated partner does not sign the grant agreement, cannot charge costs, does not need legal validation and does not count towards the minimum of three beneficiaries from three countries. It must still register in the Participant Register before the application is submitted.
In Area C, TenneT could provide grid-storage requirements as an associated partner.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 5 · B — Eligibility, Associated partners
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Registration, Consortium roles and Associated partners
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 101–105 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-04-Two-Stage-D2-07

cards.title: Receive funding
cards.question: Can TenneT receive funding, and which funding rate or cost rules apply?
cards.answer:
Yes: as a beneficiary TenneT could receive up to 100% of its eligible costs, built into a lump sum.
This topic is a research and innovation action (a project that creates new knowledge or tests the feasibility of a new technology, up to small-scale prototypes), for which the maximum rate is 100% for all participants, including companies. The grant is a lump sum fixed from a detailed budget and paid against completed work packages. The expected EU contribution is around EUR 4.8 million per project, for the whole consortium. The call sets no Dutch national rules.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · G — Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 101–105 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-04-Two-Stage-D2-07, Specific conditions

cards.title: TenneT's likely contribution
cards.question: What contribution would make TenneT credible and useful within the project?
cards.answer:
Only in Area C could TenneT contribute, by specifying grid-storage requirements, such as multi-hour duration and services, and assessing system integration potential.
This is our interpretation. Area C asks grid-storage solutions to show cost-effective system integration and multi-hour support for renewables and grid flexibility. TenneT's experience with battery operators, such as the time-dependent transmission rights contract with Lion Storage, could inform what grid use cases require. At TRL 4–5 the work is laboratory research, so TenneT's input would be small.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 101–105 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-04-Two-Stage-D2-07, Scope

project_requirements.title: Innovation
project_requirements.question: What type of innovation must the project develop?

cards.title: Innovation threshold
cards.question: Must the project produce genuinely new knowledge or technology, or may it integrate and apply existing solutions?
cards.answer: The project must go beyond the state of the art with genuinely new battery concepts and materials, benchmarked against current technology.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 101–105 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-04-Two-Stage-D2-07, Scope and Expected Outcome

cards.title: Innovation object
cards.question: In what must the project innovate?
cards.answer: Technology: battery chemistries, advanced materials, cell-level concepts and structural integration.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 101–105 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-04-Two-Stage-D2-07, Scope

cards.title: Development stages
cards.question: Which development stages must the project cover?
cards.answer: Research and laboratory validation of concepts, with assessments of scalability and manufacturability; no demonstration.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 101–105 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-04-Two-Stage-D2-07, Scope and Specific conditions

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?
cards.answer:
Activities are expected to reach TRL 4–5 by the end of the project and may start at any TRL.
TRL 4 is technology validated in a laboratory; TRL 5 is technology validated in a relevant environment.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 101–105 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-04-Two-Stage-D2-07, Specific conditions, Technology Readiness Level
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 15 · B — Technology Readiness Levels

project_requirements.title: Work
project_requirements.question: Which activities or work structure must the project cover?

cards.title: Demonstration
cards.question: Where and under which conditions must the solution be demonstrated?
cards.answer: No real-world demonstration is required: validation in the laboratory or a relevant environment, at TRL 4–5.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 101–105 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-04-Two-Stage-D2-07, Specific conditions and Expected Outcome

cards.title: Integration
cards.question: How must the activities fit together and with existing systems?

cards.title: Evidence
cards.question: What must the demonstration prove?
cards.answer:
Each area has quantified targets, and all results must be compared with a state-of-the-art benchmark.
- Area A: state-of-the-art benchmark for lithium-ion and sodium-ion batteries, and component cost below EUR 35 per kWh
- Area B: above 500 Wh/kg and/or power density beyond the benchmark
- Area C (grid): system cost target below EUR 50 per kWh and multi-hour storage support
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 101–105 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-04-Two-Stage-D2-07, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: User participation
cards.question: How must users take part in the project?

cards.title: Safety and cybersecurity
cards.question: Which safety, cybersecurity or data requirements must the project meet?
cards.answer:
Safety is a mandatory assessment: enhanced safety, thermal management, performance monitoring and predictive diagnostics; the call sets no cybersecurity rule.
The Safe and Sustainable by Design framework should be used as reference. If satellite data are used, Copernicus and/or Galileo/EGNOS must be used.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 101–105 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-04-Two-Stage-D2-07, Specific conditions and Scope

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
About 10 projects of around EUR 4.8 million each can be funded from the topic budget of EUR 48 million.
- Total project size: not stated
- Grant request: around EUR 4.8 million per project, for the whole consortium; other amounts may be requested and selected
- Funding form: lump sum (a fixed amount set from a detailed budget and paid against completed work packages)
Final budgets may change by up to 20% after evaluation.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 43–44 · Call BATTERIES and MOBILITY (HORIZON-CL5-2027-04-Two-Stage), Overview of this call
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 101–105 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-04-Two-Stage-D2-07, Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 29 · F — Budget flexibility

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
The single rate for all participants, including companies such as TenneT, is up to 100% of eligible costs.
- Co-financing conditions: none required by the call; every beneficiary can be reimbursed up to all its eligible costs
Grants may not produce a profit: any surplus of revenue plus grant over costs is deducted from the final grant.
For lump sum grants the rate is applied when the lump sum is calculated and does not appear in the grant agreement.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · G — Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
The grant is a lump sum fixed from a detailed budget table, which must still follow the normal cost-eligibility rules.
- Eligible costs: the detailed budget table must contain only costs that would be eligible under an actual-cost grant (personnel, subcontracting, purchases, other direct costs), because the lump sum must approximate the costs actually incurred
- Overheads and VAT: indirect costs are included in the lump sum calculation at the standard 25% flat rate of direct costs (excluding subcontracting)
- Subcontracting or equipment: purchases and subcontracting must give best value for money and be free of conflicts of interest; ineligible costs in the budget table can lead to a reduced grant, even late in the project
Payment depends on completing the work packages, not on proving the costs.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents, lump sum grant proposals
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 32 · G — Budget categories and cost eligibility rules

cards.title: Cash flow and financial exposure
cards.answer:
Partners normally receive a large advance after signing, minus a 5–8% contribution to a shared insurance fund, then interim payments.
- Payment model: pre-financing (an advance) of normally 160% of the average EU funding per reporting period, then interim payments linked to periodic reports, and a final payment after the final report fixes the grant
- Retention or guarantee: 5% to 8% of the maximum grant is deducted from the pre-financing and paid into the mutual insurance mechanism (a fund covering sums that cannot be recovered from beneficiaries)
- Financial reporting or audit: depending on grant size and type of beneficiary, a certificate on the financial statements may be required; each beneficiary is liable only for its own debts
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 32–33 · G — Reporting & payment arrangements, Certificates, Liability regime for recoveries

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
Two stages (a short, anonymous outline first; only consortia that pass are invited to send a full proposal), through the EU Funding & Tenders Portal.
- Stage 1 — Outline proposal: 14 April 2027, 17:00 Brussels time; at most 10 pages, evaluated blindly, so organisation names, acronyms, logos and staff names must not appear in the abstract or Part B
- Stage 2 — Full proposal: 7 October 2027, 17:00 Brussels time, by invitation only after passing stage 1; Part B of at most 45 pages (the limit for lump sum research and innovation actions) with a detailed lump sum budget table
- Opening: 15 December 2026
- Additional procedure: none; the Commission may open the call up to one month earlier or later and delay deadlines by up to two months
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 43–44 · Call BATTERIES and MOBILITY (HORIZON-CL5-2027-04-Two-Stage), Overview of this call
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 101–105 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-04-Two-Stage-D2-07, Specific conditions, Admissibility conditions and Procedure
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 3–4, 28 · A — Admissibility, Page limits; F — Evaluation procedure

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
The call sets no duration or start date: both are fixed in the grant agreement.
- Maximum duration: not set by the call; the grant agreement states the duration in months, and extensions are possible only exceptionally
- Required start: normally after the grant agreement is signed; an earlier start is possible only exceptionally, for duly justified reasons and with the granting authority's agreement
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 30–31 · G — Starting date & project duration

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
Indicatively, stage 1 results come about 3 months after its deadline, and the grant is signed about 8 months after the stage 2 deadline.
- Expected invitation or assessment result: about 3 months after the stage 1 deadline (indicative)
- Funding decision: about 5 months after the stage 2 deadline (indicative)
- Grant agreement: about 8 months after the stage 2 deadline (indicative)
- Conditions before starting: an invitation to grant preparation is not yet a funding commitment, since legal entity validation, financial capacity and exclusion checks follow; the partners must sign a written consortium agreement
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 30 · F — Indicative timetable for evaluation and for signature of the grant agreement
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 29 · F — No commitment to provide funding
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Consortium agreement

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
The proposal must be complete, submitted electronically before the deadline, and within the page limit; incomplete applications are rejected.
- Application form: Part A (administrative data and a summary budget, filled in online) and Part B (the technical description, uploaded as a PDF) through the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, using the forms inside the submission system; Part B is limited to 45 pages; the stage 1 outline is limited to 10 pages
- Budget: the summary budget in Part A and a detailed budget table, which is the basis for the lump sum
- Mandatory annexes: a plan for the exploitation and dissemination of results, including communication activities (not needed at stage 1), and the ethics self-assessment
- Partner documents: the coordinator confirms at submission that it has the mandate to act for all applicants; every participant signs a declaration of honour before the grant is signed
- Registration: every beneficiary, affiliated entity and associated partner needs a participant identification code (PIC, a number from the EU Participant Register) before submission; validation of beneficiaries follows at grant preparation
- Parallel submission: none
- Blind first stage: no organisation names, acronyms, logos or staff names in the stage 1 abstract and Part B
- Lump sum: the detailed budget table at stage 2 is used to fix the lump sum
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 3–4 · A — Admissibility, Page limits
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 5 · B — Entities eligible to participate
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 15 · B — Ethics
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Registration
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 101–105 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-04-Two-Stage-D2-07, Specific conditions

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Independent experts score three criteria out of 5; a proposal needs 3 on each and 10 in total.
- Evaluation criteria: Excellence (clear, ambitious objectives beyond the state of the art; sound methodology), Impact (credible pathways to the expected outcomes; dissemination and exploitation measures) and Quality and efficiency of the implementation (work plan, risks, resources, capacity of each partner)
- Stage 1: only Excellence and Impact are scored, each needing at least 4; the overall stage 1 threshold is set so that about three times the budget goes through to stage 2, normally 8 or 8.5
- Thresholds: at least 3 out of 5 for each criterion and 10 out of 15 overall
- Ranking rules: equal scores are separated first by whether a proposal covers aspects of the call not covered by higher-ranked ones, then by the Excellence score, then Impact, then gender balance among lead researchers and geographical diversity
- Budget assessment: the grant awarded may be lower than requested, and topic budgets may change by up to 20% after evaluation
- Portfolio rule: besides ranking order, at least the highest-ranked proposal in each of the three areas is funded, if it passes all thresholds
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 23–26 · D — Award criteria, Scores and weighting, Two-stage calls
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 28–29 · F — Evaluation procedure and ranking, Budget flexibility
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 31 · G — Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
A blind first stage, one area per proposal, a portfolio rule and the possible JRC role are specific to this topic.
- Exception — blind evaluation: stage 1 proposals must be anonymous
- Conditional — area: contribute to one of the three areas and meet its targets
- Exception — ranking: the top proposal of each area is funded if it passes the thresholds
- Exception — Joint Research Centre: may join after selection without taking part in the proposal
- Conditional — results transfer: the granting authority may object to transfers or exclusive licensing for 4 years after the project
- Conditional — partnership reporting: report to Batt4EU and IAM4EU
- Recommended: use the Safe and Sustainable by Design framework
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 101–105 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-04-Two-Stage-D2-07, Specific conditions and Scope
